title: Currently testing Antigravity + Godot MCP. Looking to create a 2.5d Contra type game.
author: Secret_Slide_1357
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1pmtbpo/video/6890n83nf97g1/player

I originally got Unity and tried to just follow steps from Gemini but that was taking way too much time. I figured I'd setup the Godot MCP instead see how it works.

Took about 20 minutes to get the MCP working, that was fairly simple. Got some free assets packs and managed to get my player moving and shooting properly. Will keep you updated on the whole process.

comments.author: Pretend-Park6473
comments.body: What does MCP do? Antigravity (Sonnet 4.5) works fine on editing Godot project without MCP.

replies.author: Secret_Slide_1357
replies.body: Oh yeah? how so? Just editing project files directly there?

replies.author: Pretend-Park6473
replies.body:
Yeah, add the directory to the agent manager and it pretty much does everything

https://preview.redd.it/vqhuxkcm5c7g1.png?width=515&format=png&auto=webp&s=271831ac8cbb12037dfec57e0899eb70114ae3dd

replies.author: Secret_Slide_1357
replies.body:
Right well I just realized it usually doesnt even use the mcp, I just seen it use it to create nodes through the mcp or create a scene. Not sure if its worth it tbh. 

One this for sure Sonnet 4.5 performs wayyyyyy better than gemini3 pro in Godot it's not even comparable. Thank God you mentionned it.

replies.author: SoMuchMango
replies.body:
Yeah, i think MCP with Godot is a bit of overkill as all the Godot files are understandable flat files, so SCP is just formalising stuff that is accessible by editing files. LLMs can easily "understand" how to node without having named function for that.

  
 Am i right?

replies.author: Pretend-Park6473
replies.body: Yeah I think Godot MCP can run debug

comments.author: beneficialdiet18
comments.body: Did you use blender for the assets or did you get pre animated ones?

comments.author: __Maximum__
comments.body: Are you sure antigravity is a good idea? I would recommend trying an alternative to compare it. In my few attempts, it failed on tasks that gemini 3.0 could eqsily do elsewhere, say on aistudio.

replies.author: Secret_Slide_1357
replies.body: Well so far so good but I did notice that antigravity tends to underperform compared to regular web Gemini copy and paste.

replies.author: __Maximum__
replies.body: Perhaps roo code or similar would work better. Gemini cli also did not do wonders for me but still better than antigravity even though it used gemini 2.5 pro sometimes instead of 3.0 pro.

replies.author: Secret_Slide_1357
replies.body:
Yeah probably, I managed to get stuff done with Antigravity Gemini pro high but as soon as it started struggling I just went back to web G3P and I could immediately see how better it performed. 

Some tasks took 2-3 attempts to achieve with AG, on the web G3P it could handle multiple tasks at once on first try. 

The copy and paste is the downside but ah well...

comments.author: op_app_pewer
comments.body:
Is the 2.5d important? Otherwise you could do all of it in dreamforge.ai including animations^^
(Although we don’t do backgrounds well yet! I could spend some time getting that to work for you if you want though^^)

The coding agent itself is much better than Gemini 3 and sprite+animation gen are also great^^ 

Here is something I made in 5 prompts: https://dreamforge.ai/play/0a25d9-create-a-complete-vampire-survivors-style-arena-

I guess if the 2.5d is kind of 2d sprites in a sidescrolling 3d world that should work (like the ninja turtles game on snes)

replies.author: Secret_Slide_1357
replies.body: I don't remember but it was not very useful. Just a regular AI assisted IDE like cursor did most of the work.
